info.name: HRM Employee Mobile API (v1)
info.description: Employee mobile app API. Import the environment too, set email and password, then run "Login" first: it saves the token for every other request. Leave types saves leave_type_id; Payslips / Assets lists save payslip_id / asset_id; applying for leave saves leave_id. Full documentation: README.md in the same folder.

request.description:
Sign in with e-mail and password. Saves the token for every other request.

401 wrong e-mail/password, 403 account cannot use the app (deactivated, login disabled, past last working day, not an employee), 429 after 5 wrong tries (1 minute).

urlencoded.description: Optional: shown as the token name

response.name: Logged in
Wrong password
Invalid e-mail
Login disabled by HR

request.description: E-mails a 6-digit code (valid 15 minutes, 5 tries, single use). The answer is the same whether or not the e-mail exists. 3 requests per 10 minutes per e-mail.

response.name: Code sent
Too many requests

request.description: Optional: check the code before showing the new-password screen. A wrong code counts as one of the 5 tries.

response.name: Correct
Wrong code
Expired / used / too many tries

request.description:
Sets a new password with the e-mailed code. Signs the account out of every device (all tokens revoked) - log in again afterwards.

Password: at least 8 characters, at most 50.

response.name: Changed
Expired code
Passwords differ

request.description: Signed in: change the password. Other devices are signed out; this token keeps working.

response.name: Changed
Wrong current password

request.description: Ends this token.

response.name: Logged out

request.description:
The signed-in employee: personal and job details, emergency contacts, today's shift.

`modules` lists the modules this person has (`key` never changes, `name` is the label), for showing or hiding screens. HR and admin accounts get more, e.g. `biometric`, `employee_management`.

response.name: Profile
No token

request.description:
Updates only the fields sent (multipart, because of the photo). Name, e-mail, department, designation, manager and employment dates are HR-managed and cannot be changed here.

marital_status: single, married, widower, widow, separate, divorced, engaged. marriage_date is required when married and cleared otherwise.
Answers with the full profile, as GET /me.

response.name: Validation

request.description:
Clocked in? On a break? Today's sessions and breaks, and whether photo / location are required.

Also returns can_clock_in (Attendance Settings switch), office_radius_m (null when the radius is not checked) and offices[] for the office picker.

response.name: Clocked in, on a break
Not clocked in

request.description:
Clock in with photo and location (multipart/form-data). Pick an image file for "photo".

Same rules as the website clock-in (Attendance Settings): photo/location requirement, "employees may clock in" switch (403 when off), IP list and office radius (403 outside; both skipped for work_from_type = home). The radius is measured from location_id, else the employee's office, else the default office.

formdata.description: Optional: the office picked, from offices[] in GET /attendance/today (as on the website)
Camera image (jpg/png/webp, max 2 MB). Required when /attendance/today says requirements.photo = mandatory.
Alternative to photo: the image as base64

response.name: Clocked in
Already clocked in
Outside the office radius
Self clock-in switched off

request.description:
Clock out with photo and location (multipart/form-data). Ends a running break too.

The IP and office-radius rules apply as on the website (skipped for work_from_type = home).

formdata.description: Optional: the office picked, from offices[] in GET /attendance/today (as on the website)
Camera image (jpg/png/webp, max 2 MB). Required when /attendance/today says requirements.photo = mandatory.
Alternative to photo: the image as base64

response.name: Clocked out
Not clocked in
Outside the office radius

request.description: Start a lunch / tea / other break. Recorded only: worked hours are not reduced.

response.name: Break started
A break is already running
Not clocked in

request.description: End the running break.

response.name: Break ended
No break running

request.description:
Day by day over any period up to 92 days, newest first, counted exactly as payroll counts it. Defaults: from = 1st of this month, to = today.

status filters the days (present, absent, paid_leave, holiday, week_off, half_day, ...). Each day has the same fields as /attendance/calendar.

request.description:
Applies for the employee's own leave, always as Pending, and starts the approval steps (manager → department head → HR, as Leave Settings tick them) with the usual e-mails/bells.

duration: single | multiple | first_half | second_half. leave_date for single / half days; from_date + to_date for multiple. Holidays in the range are left out.
Checked as on the website: type allowed for the employee, Earned Leave service years, the type's Rules (notice, back-dating, most days, document), balance and monthly limit (types that may not go over).

409 when a day already has pending/approved leave (the website would silently reject the old one; the app refuses instead), or a full day already has a clock-in - send mark_leave_anyway = 1 to apply anyway.
files[]: optional documents (jpg, png, webp, pdf, doc, docx; 5 MB each; up to 5).
